title: Restricted pro-etale affine-line counit
statement:
Let $A=A_{E,n}$, $T$ be Noetherian with $\ell$ invertible and $\ell^{r+1}A=0$. Define the affine-line left functor as exact chart extension by zero followed by proper derived direct image. The right-object comparison is the canonical scheme pullback comparison followed by pullback of the canonical projective tensor-source comparison. Restrict the projective counit by the actual open-extension counit to obtain the affine-line counit on every bounded-below etale-origin coefficient. The infinity divisor is Cartier on every base by its standard coordinate description.

proof.text: Keep the canonical functors, pullback comparison and restricted counit exactly as constructed in the Lean definitions. For the remaining infinityCartier assertion put p : P^1_T -> T and i : T -> P^1_T for infinity. The existing ProjectiveLine.infinity_over gives i followed by p equal to the identity. Since p is separated, the existing closed-immersion cancellation theorem makes i a closed immersion.

For J = ker(i), the canonical factorization i = toImage(i) followed by J.subschemeι identifies T with the closed subscheme cut out by J: toImage(i) is an isomorphism for a closed immersion. Cancel toImage(i) in the section identity to get J.subschemeι followed by p = inverse(toImage(i)). Consequently this composite is an isomorphism, hence finite, flat and locally of finite presentation. These arguments also apply when T is empty.

The proved source-library instance ProjectiveLine.smoothOfRelativeDimension_one gives smoothness of p in relative dimension one over the arbitrary base T. Apply the finite-flat implication of [lem-pc-cartier-criterion], implemented by Scheme.IdealSheafData.isInvertible_of_isFinite_of_flat, to J and the three properties from the preceding step. This proves J.IsInvertible with no Noetherian or coefficient hypothesis.
